_source: app.notion.com ComCom > Projects, 'on-going projects' table view, Created time column, 2026-08-06. Read-only: wheel-scrolled the table sideways until the column painted, then read the text-bearing element's computed styles (not the cell box — that reports the container's inherited 16px/24px).

format._reads: ko-KR, long month, 12-hour with 오전/오후, no seconds, no leading zero on the hour. The property carries no date_format of its own (its config is {}), so this is Notion's default for created_time under a Korean UI.

_dataGap: The original's rows were created over months (May–August 2026 in the rows on screen). Our seed inserted all 251 rows at once, so db_rows.created_at spans three minutes on 2026-08-06 and the whole column reads as one date. The per-row created_time is NOT in the saved source data (rows-normalized.json carries only cells+id; rows.json is truncated), so closing that gap needs a fresh read-only fetch from the original.
